newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Dynamis Energetica goes on sale today.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Dynamis Energetica goes on sale today.

text.p: Four investors will compete in today's bid for Brazilian power utility Dynamis Energetica which is being auctioned with a base price of 100 million reais ($94.3 million) on the Rio bourse, a stock exchange spokeswoman said.
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) will be selling a total of 295,525 common shares in the power utility, formerly known as Nacional Energetica, she said.

Investment bank Bozano Simonsen, Belgian holding company Tractebel, power utility Escelsa and the Serra da Mesa consortium, consisting of Brazil's Bradesco, Votorantim and Camargo Correia, have prequalified to participate in the auction.
It is the second attempt to sell the company which has a 51.54 percent stake in the 1,223-megawatt Serra da Mesa hydroelectric plant on the Tocantins River in northern Brazil.
Serra de Mesa is due to open in April 1998 and should generate revenues of $100 to $140 million annually.

Dynamis Energetica has already invested 556 million reais ($524.5 million) in the plant. The total cost of the project is estimated at approximately 2 billion reais ($1.89 billion) of which Dynamis is investing a total of 860 million reais ($811.3 million).
An August 15 auction of then Nacional Energetica failed to attract any buyers when the firm went up for sale at a minimum price of 168.4 million reais ($158.9 million).
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151 ($ = 1.052 Brazilian Reals)
